claims.claim: Subsection (a) authorizes the TSA Administrator, not later than 60 days after enactment, to establish a pilot program at airports to expedite access to security screening for traveling active-duty military personnel and accompanying family members.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration

claims.claim: The Administrator may carry out this subsection only to the extent such access does not compromise security protocols.

claims.note: (c),(d),(e) each open with "If the Administrator establishes the pilot program under subsection (a)."

claims.claim: Subsection (b) sets three security requirements the Administrator must carry out.
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator shall carry out the following
claims.note: "shall carry out the following" = mandatory; three items.

claims.claim: (1) ensure each passenger is screened per the Secure Flight vetting status, in accordance with paragraph (2) of section 44903(j) of title 49.
claims.sourceSpan: in accordance with paragraph (2) of section 44903(j) of title 49, United States Code

claims.claim: (2) prevent individuals carrying out screening functions under section 44901 from allowing any passenger into a TSA PreCheck or other expedited lane unless the passenger has a boarding pass indicating eligibility for TSA PreCheck or such other expedited screening.
claims.sourceSpan: Prevent individuals carrying out screening functions under section 44901 of such from allowing any passenger into a TSA PreCheck or other expedited security screening lane
claims.note: Accurate rendering: 44901 correctly bound to the screening functions; eligibility bound to PreCheck.

claims.claim: (3) permit local Administration management to open or close checkpoint lanes and reallocate available resources as needed to maximize security effectiveness and efficiency based on passenger volume.
claims.sourceSpan: Permit local Administration management to open or close checkpoint lanes and reallocate available resources as needed to maximize security effectiveness and efficiency based on passenger volume

claims.claim: The three requirements preserve Secure Flight-based screening, enforce the boarding-pass-eligibility precondition, and preserve local flexibility.
claims.sourceSpan: unless such passenger has received a boarding pass indicating eligibility for TSA PreCheck or such other expedited security screening
